explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/779 (Deaconescu): for n > 1, with p_1 < ⋯ < p_n the first n primes and P their product, does there always exist a prime p with p_n < p < P such that P + p is prime? The Lean statement is index-shifted: for n ≥ 1, P = ∏_{i ≤ n} nth Prime i is the product of the first n+1 primes (so at least two primes, matching n > 1 in the source), and it asserts a prime p with nth Prime n < p < P and P + p prime, where nth Prime n is the largest prime in the product. The shift is noted in the docstring. Stated as a conjecture without the question tag, a tagging nuance only. Faithful.
